The primary outcome is true through MET plus tepotinib in Group B.
Group B requires "WHO grade IV glioma (glioblastoma or gliosarcoma)" with no IDH requirement for glioblastoma. C8 treats "grade 4/IV ... glioma without an IDH requirement" as historical.

The GBM group is "At first, second or third recurrence of glioblastoma". The other groups have brain metastases ("newly-diagnosed or recurrent brain metastases"), which is advanced metastatic disease and therefore recurrent under C10. No group is newly diagnosed primary disease in first-line treatment.

note: The registered arm labels (Group A tepotinib alone; Group B tepotinib + osimertinib) do not match the description (A = brain metastases, B = recurrent GBM on tepotinib alone, C = EGFR+ NSCLC on tepotinib + osimertinib). Under D31-C3 the regimen is that of the GBM group (monotherapy); combination_partners ['osimertinib'] is left as the coders agreed (C2 lists drugs given with the candidate, here in Group C). D31-A1 makes the Group C EGFR row exploratory_correlative; the coder A IDH row ("also eligible") is an optional route (D31-A2) and does not count. treatment_setting 'both' would be defensible if XL reads 'newly-diagnosed brain metastases' as newly diagnosed; no D31 convention covers it.

revisions.reason: EGFR mutation is an entry requirement only for the NSCLC Group C; Group B (glioblastoma) requires only "MET alteration identified through molecular testing".
The GBM arm is Group B, "To determine RP2D of tepotinib in patients with GLIOBLASTOMA with MET alterations" (tepotinib alone); osimertinib is given only in the NSCLC Group C.
